claim: Polonnaruwa's rise should be treated as multi-causal: it was already a strategically important provincial centre before becoming the capital; its inland position, relation to the Mahaweli, agricultural/hydraulic potential, Chola-era administrative use, and easier connection to the eastern seaboard all increased its value. Current evidence supports Gokanna/Trincomalee access as one contributor to that value, but not as a demonstrated primary cause of the shift from Anuradhapura.
bounded_by: Do not narrate a simple seventh-century Bay-of-Bengal trade shift as the cause of capital relocation. Chola conquest, defence, pre-existing strategic status, irrigation/agriculture and dynastic choices remain independent mechanisms.
notes: Run49 resolves the strong version of the Gokanna hypothesis negatively while retaining a bounded positive contribution claim.
